catalog_quote: テンボ語の声調については特徴的なことが 2 つある。1 つは、声調の調値がバンツー祖語や周辺言語と比べて逆転していることである（梶 1994, Kaji 1996）。もう 1 つは、名詞類の声調のパターンが単語を構成するモーラ数が増えるに従って等比級数的に増えていく無制限タイプであることである（梶 1978, 2001b）。さらに、声調実現の単位が音節ではなくモーラである点、また単独形の声調が基本となるというのもテンボ語の特徴である。[...] テンボ語の基本声調は他の多くのアフリカ諸語同様、高平板調 H (high) と低平板調 L (low) の 2 つである。尤も、音声的には H と L の組み合わせにより (1a) のように下降調 F (falling) と (1b) のように上昇調 R (rising) が生じる。[...] テンボ語には母音の長短の区別はない。かつての母音の長短の区別は失われ 1 モーラ化している。[...] テンボ語の TRU は音節ではなくモーラである。

sweep_summary: Tembo (Kitembo) is not in the catalog. The three title-keyword items are all false attachments: Philippson 1991 (thesis on East African Bantu tone/accent, already held by the project under bemb1257 with a text) has zero mentions of Tembo — its Group I sample is nande, konzo, hunde, shi, fuliru (Tableau 1, p. 70), and it links to temb1270 only via Maho's autotranslation of j.d.53 (Shi); it says Group I languages are tonal (Hunde reduces HH to HL, p. 412) and that penultimate demarcative accent replaced tone only in Group III (Nyoro/Tooro). Möhlig 1969 (two duplicate Glottolog records) deals with Dciriku, Hehe, Chaga and Shi, is print-only (ZDMG Suppl. I; no digital copy found on MENAdoc or elsewhere), and is attached to Tembo by a computerized assignment. The substantive Tembo literature is Kaji's first-hand work (1978, 1994, 2001, 2021, all open and already held by the project), which uniformly describes Tembo as a polymoraic tone language (H/L on each mora; contrasted with accentual Haya and bound-accent Swahili) and never posits word stress; Kaji 1996 JALL remains paywalled. Best statement: Kaji 2001, p. 37 English summary.fr, HAL API, MENAdoc, De Gruyter) only.

new_statements.quote: テンボ語の声調については特徴的なことが 2 つある。1 つは、声調の調値がバンツー祖語や周辺言語と比べて逆転していることである（梶 1994, Kaji 1996）。もう 1 つは、名詞類の声調のパターンが単語を構成するモーラ数が増えるに従って等比級数的に増えていく無制限タイプであることである（梶 1978, 2001b）。さらに、声調実現の単位が音節ではなくモーラである点、また単独形の声調が基本となるというのもテンボ語の特徴である。[...] テンボ語の基本声調は他の多くのアフリカ諸語同様、高平板調 H (high) と低平板調 L (low) の 2 つである。
new_statements.translation: Two things are characteristic of Tembo tone. One is that the tone values are reversed compared with Proto-Bantu and the neighbouring languages (Kaji 1994, 1996). The other is that the tone patterns of nominals are of the unrestricted type, increasing geometrically as the number of moras making up the word increases (Kaji 1978, 2001b). Further characteristics of Tembo are that the unit of tone realization is the mora, not the syllable, and that isolation-form tone is basic. [...] The basic tones of Tembo are, as in many other African languages, two: level high H and level low L.

I read the surrounding sections myself: sec. 1.2 adds F/R as H+L combinations, tone on word-in…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Tembo is described as a pure ('unrestricted', 2^n-pattern) mora-counting tone language with lexical H vs L on every mora (F and R as HL/LH combinations), downdrift but no downstep, and no vowel-length contrast; Kaji (1978, 2001, 2021) explicitly contrasts it with pitch accent/accentual Bantu languages. None of his opened descriptions mentions word stress, dynamic accent or penultimate prominence for Tembo.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. (Tonal notes: word-initial syllabic nasal bears its own tone; rising tone is realized as H word-initially; some patterns exceed 2^n, e.g. FH, LFL.)
new_statements.domain_note: Isolation (citation) forms are stated to be tonally basic; description is of word-level lexical tone, mainly Bunyakiri dialect, tone said to be identical across dialects.
new_statements.identity_note: All of Kaji's data are Tembo (Échítembo) of eastern DRC, glottocode temb1270, ISO tbt; the 2021 chapter states examples are mainly from the western Bunyakiri dialect and that tone is identical across the four dialects (Mbugu, Buloho, Bunyakiri, Ufamandu). Kaji notes Maho's JD531 code conflates Tembo with Shi (JD53); Kaji himself uses J.57. Not to be confused with Tembo (Motembo) of Equateur (tmv).

new_statements.quote: With Tembo it is demonstrated that in this language each mora in principle should be marked either as high, low, falling or rising (the last two being combinations of high and low). The number of partterns increases in geometric progression. Tembo, therefore, can be characterized as a polymoraic tone language. In Haya, however, the number of tone patterns increases in arithmetic progression, as a function of the number of the syllables in the stem. High tone has become accentual in nature in Haya, in which only one high tone syllable per word is permitted in isolation. [...] and a bound accent language (Swahili).
new_statements.translation: (English original; the body of the paper is Japanese)
new_statements.citation: Kaji, Shigeki (梶茂樹) (2001). バンツー諸語の音調－そのタイプ－ / Tonal types of Bantu languages. 音声研究 (Journal of the Phonetic Society of Japan) 5(1): 37-45. doi:10.24467/onseikenkyu.5.1_37
new_statements.reading: The one first-hand description of Tembo (Kaji, own fieldwork since 1976) classifies it as a polymoraic tone language: lexical H/L on every mora, patterns multiplying geometrically with length, explicitly opposed to accentual Haya and bound-accent Swahili. No word stress, culminative accent or fixed prominence position is posited for Tembo in any source read (Kaji 1978, 1994, 2001, 2021). If Tembo is added to the catalog, the classification supported is 'tone language, no word stress/fixed accent', with Kaji 2001 (or Kaji 2021 ch. 6) as the deciding source. Neither title-keyword item in this search of works with stress in the title says anything about Tembo: Philippson 1991 does not include Tembo in its sample and Möhlig 1969 concerns Shi/Dciriku/Hehe/Chaga; both are attached to temb1270 by Maho-code autotranslation of j.d.53 (Shi).

tone_statements.citation: Kabucungu Hand-jinga 2005. Verb structure in Kitembo. MA (Translation Studies) linguistics project, Nairobi Evangelical Graduate School of Theology. x+65 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Like most Bantu languages, Kitembo is tonal. The tone is a very important feature of Kitembo because it helps hearers to differentiate the words the speaker is saying. It has two main tones, High (H) and Low (L). High tone is represented by an acute accent ( ) while the low is represented by a grave accent ( ` ). (1) mwàná ‘child’ (2) múlùmé ‘man’ In addition, there are many words that are phonologically identical except for their tones. (3) chíróngò ‘dry soil’ (4) chíròngò ‘yam’ (5) músí ‘village’ (6) mùsí ‘smoke’
tone_statements.locator: sec. 1.1.4.2 'Tone', p. 8; grammatical and conditioned tone pp. 9-10
tone_statements.summary: 2 tones H/L, lexical and grammatical (tense marked by tone on subject prefix and stem); HL/LH contours; H lowered after L in HLH; no stress statement.

tone_statements.citation: 梶茂樹 (Kaji, Shigeki) 1998. テンボ語（旧ザイール、バンツー系）：多音節語の声調言語 [Tembo (former Zaire, Bantu): a tone language with polysyllabic words]. 発表要旨 (presentation abstract), 重点共同研究プロジェクト「音韻に関する通言語的研究」(META-PHONOLOGY), 1998年度第1回研究会, 1998-05-09. Tokyo: ILCAA, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. 1 p. (HTML).
tone_statements.quote: テンボ語の基本的声調は、H(高平板調)とL(低平板調)であるが、この分布を以上の構造に合わせて見ると、 [...] の様に、2モーラ(音節)語では2×2＝4、3モーラ(音節)語では2×2×2＝8のパターンが見られる。さらに4モーラ(音節)語でも、2×2×2×2＝16のパターンがある。従って、パターン数は、声調数2を公比とする等比級数として表すことができ(F(n)＝2n)、テンボ語は、各モーラ(音節)に声調を指定しなければならない声調言語ということになる。
tone_statements.translation: The basic tones of Tembo are H (high level) and L (low level); looking at their distribution over the structures above, [...] as shown, 2-mora (syllable) words have 2x2=4 patterns and 3-mora (syllable) words 2x2x2=8. Four-mora (syllable) words likewise have 2x2x2x2=16 patterns. The number of patterns can thus be expressed as a geometric progression with the number of tones, 2, as ratio (F(n)=2^n), which makes Tembo a tone language in which tone must be specified for every mora (syllable).
tone_statements.locator: abstract body, paragraphs 3-4 (between them the pattern table H-H.. L-LL)
tone_statements.summary: Two level tones H/L assigned per mora, unrestricted 2^n lexical patterns on nouns, H noun prefixes (reversal relative to Proto-Bantu).

tone_statements.quote: 音の高低によって単語の意味が違うし、また時制なども違ってくるのだ。 [...] 特に、テンボ語とレガ語では隣接言語でありながら、声調は全く逆になっている。
tone_statements.translation: Word meanings differ according to pitch, and so do tenses and the like. [...] In particular, Tembo and Lega, though neighbouring languages, have completely reversed tones.

tone_statements.summary: Lexical and grammatical (tense) tone; Tembo tones reversed relative to neighbouring Lega.

sources.quote: The Bantu languages of Africa show various tone types, ranging from pure tone languages to non-tonal languages. In this paper the author analyses the tone system of nouns in two languges: Tembo (J 57, eastern Congo) and Haya (J 22, northwestern Tanzania). With Tembo it is demonstrated that in this language each mora in principle should be marked either as high, low, falling or rising (the last two being combinations of high and low). The number of partterns increases in geometric progression. Tembo, therefore, can be characterized as a polymoraic tone language.
sources.note: First-hand (Kaji's own 1976-77 fieldwork): Tembo is a polymoraic tone language — every mora bears lexical H/L (or F/R), tone patterns multiply geometrically with word length — explicitly contrasted in the same summary with Haya (H 'has become accentual in nature', one H per word) and Swahili ('a bound accent language'). No word stress or culminative accent is posited for Tembo; no stress position is stated anywhere.

sources.note: Typological abstract on Tembo tone: two basic tones H (high level) and L (low level); nouns prefix+stem CV-CV / CV-CV(N)CV; every mora (syllable) must be lexically specified, giving 2x2=4 patterns for 2-mora words, 8 for 3-mora, 16 for 4-mora (F(n)=2^n), so Tembo is a tone language of the type that specifies tone per mora; noun prefixes are mostly H (tone reversal vs Proto-Bantu L), L prefixes being loans or vowel-initial-stem reflexes, so prefix tone must also be specified ('true tone language' type); discussion raised an alternative tone+abstract-accent analysis.

tone.quote: テンボ語の基本的声調は、H(高平板調)とL(低平板調)であるが、この分布を以上の構造に合わせて見ると、 [...] の様に、2モーラ(音節)語では2×2＝4、3モーラ(音節)語では2×2×2＝8のパターンが見られる。さらに4モーラ(音節)語でも、2×2×2×2＝16のパターンがある。従って、パターン数は、声調数2を公比とする等比級数として表すことができ(F(n)＝2n)、テンボ語は、各モーラ(音節)に声調を指定しなければならない声調言語ということになる。
tone.locator: abstract body, paragraphs 3-4 (between them the pattern table H-H.. L-LL)
tone.translation: The basic tones of Tembo are H (high level) and L (low level); looking at their distribution over the structures above, [...] as shown, 2-mora (syllable) words have 2x2=4 patterns and 3-mora (syllable) words 2x2x2=8. Four-mora (syllable) words likewise have 2x2x2x2=16 patterns. The number of patterns can thus be expressed as a geometric progression with the number of tones, 2, as ratio (F(n)=2^n), which makes Tembo a tone language in which tone must be specified for every mora (syllable).
tone.summary: Two level tones H/L assigned per mora, unrestricted 2^n lexical patterns on nouns, H noun prefixes (reversal relative to Proto-Bantu).
